chunks.text: 4 Experiments We organize our experiments around the main design choices of Tessera. We first evaluate spatially informed gene ranking (Appendix F ), then isolate the contribution of spatial geometry and compare positional encodings under a controlled architecture. We next characterize the learned attention in terms of locality, direction sensitivity, and invariance, and assess zero-shot extrapolation beyond the spatial scale seen during training. Finally, we benchmark Tessera against existing spatial foundation models. Models, optimization, and the full experimental protocol are described in Appendix E . 4.1 Impact of spatial geometry Table 1: Impact of spatial geometry. The gain is consistent across seeds, and coordinate-permutation controls further confirm that the improvement arises from spatial geometry (Appendix E ). 4.2 Relative geometry drives performance Holding the architecture and training protocol fixed, we vary only the positional encoding.

Absolute sinusoidal encoding provides negligible improvement (+0.0005), whereas relative encodings improve Pearson correlation by +0.160–0.174 across all nine sections. RoPE performs best among the relative variants, although differences within this group are small and treated as descriptive. Beyond predictive performance, the learned attention patterns reveal distinct spatial behaviors (Fig. 2 ). Relative encodings exhibit spatial locality, while RoPE shows the strongest directional variation within a fixed distance range, in contrast to the approximately isotropic distance-only bias. Full positional-encoding results and angular analyses are provided in Appendix G , with per-section results in Table 8 . Figure 2: Direction sensitivity of learned spatial attention. Attention patterns for four positional encodings on a held-out MERSCOPE breast tissue section. Top: Mean attention weights as a function of relative cell displacement, aggregated across eight attention heads using a shared logarithmic scale. Middle: Radial attention profiles showing spatial locality. Bottom: Angular attention profiles within a fixed 25–75 μ \mu m distance range, normalized by their mean. The coefficient of variation (CV) quantifies directional sensitivity, with higher values indicating stronger anisotropy. RoPE exhibits the strongest directional variation (CV = 0.43), while the distance-only bias remains approximately isotropic (CV = 0.05). 4.3 Invariance and spatial extrapolation Directional encoding raises a natural question: tissue sections have no canonical orientation, so why preserve direction rather than enforce rotation invariance? While absolute orientation is arbitrary, relative direction can still carry biological information because local tissue organization is often anisotropic: cells at the same distance but different bearings may occupy distinct spatial contexts and therefore provide different signals about cellular state.

Translation invariance removes dependence on the arbitrary section origin while preserving these relative directional relationships. RoPE and PoPE therefore retain direction by design, whereas a distance-only bias is isotropic and cannot distinguish equally distant cells at different bearings (Appendix G ). Transformation tests confirm that RoPE and PoPE preserve attention under translation but change it under rotation, whereas the radial distance bias remains invariant to both (Fig. 4 ; Table 6 ). This relative formulation also supports spatial extrapolation. Because displacement-based encodings are defined continuously in physical space, they can be evaluated beyond the spatial scale observed during training, whereas fixed-range distance representations are tied to their predefined support. When evaluated zero-shot from N = 256 N=256 to N = 4096 N=4096 cells, RoPE and PoPE exhibit only 1.6% and 2.0% degradation, respectively, compared with 23% for the fixed-range distance bias (Fig. 3 ). The corresponding attention statistics further characterize how locality and attention concentration evolve as the spatial context expands. Additional analyses are provided in Appendix H . Additional radius sweeps, seed analyses, and validation controls are reported in Appendix I . 5 Discussion and conclusion Tessera addresses two complementary challenges in spatial representation learning: combining cell-specific expression relevance with tissue-level spatial informativeness for gene selection, and contextualizing cellular states through intercellular spatial relationships.

Its geometric inductive bias reflects a simple property of tissue organization: cellular context is relational, and equally distant cells can provide different biological information depending on their relative position and cellular state. The RoPE-based mechanism preserves this directional structure while remaining invariant to arbitrary translations of the tissue coordinate system. Importantly, we do not assume a universal tissue orientation; rather, we avoid imposing isotropy by construction, allowing locally anisotropic tissue organization to be represented. Although our current evaluation focuses on expression imputation and spatial probing, such context-aware representations could ultimately support downstream applications including spatial biomarker discovery, target prioritization, and prediction of treatment response. Appendix E Experiments All results are evaluated on held-out whole sections. We use the spatially resolved subset of SpatialCorpus-110M [ 21 ] , comprising 43 43 sections and 20,068,822 20{,}068{,}822 cells, split 30 / 4 / 9 30/4/9 by section. The nine held-out sections span two imaging technologies and seven tissues and are used only for final evaluation. Our primary statistic is the paired held-out imputation Pearson correlation, computed as a section-wise difference over n = 9 n=9 sections ( df = 8 \mathrm{df}=8 , two-sided critical value 2.306 2.306 ) and bootstrapped over sections rather than cells. All thresholds reported below were preregistered before the corresponding results were observed; the complete register, including failed criteria, is given in Appendix J . Models. Tessera combines a frozen scGPT whole-human backbone [ 7 ] with a trainable spatial attention module. For each cell, the backbone encodes K = 500 K=500 gene tokens selected through spatially informed ranking into a single 512 512 -dimensional cell representation.

The spatial attention module consists of L = 6 L=6 layers, 8 8 attention heads, and a hidden dimension of d model = 512 d_{\mathrm{model}}=512 , comprising approximately 19 19 M trainable parameters. It operates on windows of N = 256 N=256 spatially contiguous cells with a d max = 200 ​ μ ​ m d_{\max}=200\,\mu\mathrm{m} distance cutoff. The positional-encoding comparison in § 4.2 evaluates four spatial encoding strategies within this shared architecture: absolute sinusoidal embeddings of ( x , y ) (x,y) , RoPE, PoPE [ 9 ] , and an additive radial distance bias parameterized using 32 32 Gaussian basis functions [ 35 , 34 ] . We additionally include a geometry-free baseline without positional information. All five configurations share the same pretrained backbone, spatial attention architecture, training windows, masking strategy, and optimization protocol. They differ in their spatial encoding mechanisms, including the query–key parameterization associated with PoPE. We also evaluate five non-spatial predictors under matched evaluation conditions. Four non-learned baselines comprise mean_profile , neighbour_average , PCA on highly variable genes, and PCA on neighbourhood-averaged expression. The fifth baseline, scgpt_no_aggregator , uses the frozen scGPT backbone embeddings directly to assess the contribution of spatial contextualization. For the comparison with existing spatial foundation models in § 4.4 , we use the released pretrained weights and original preprocessing pipelines of Nicheformer [ 21 ] and scGPT-spatial [ 31 ] . All three models produce 512 512 -dimensional per-cell embeddings, verified at runtime, so no additional dimensionality matching is required. Training details. All models are trained with the cross-cell cloze objective: a fraction ρ = 0.1 \rho=0.1 of cells in each window is masked, and the negative-binomial loss is computed on masked cells only over a fixed decoder vocabulary of 1,245 1{,}245 genes.

For each cell, we select the top K = 500 K=500 genes according to the spatially informed ranking score in Eq. ( 14 ), with λ = 0.6 \lambda=0.6 and κ = 60 \kappa=60 fixed on development sections before held-out evaluation. The selected genes are encoded by the frozen scGPT backbone, and the resulting cell embeddings are cached for spatial model training and evaluation.. We optimise with AdamW ( β = ( 0.9 , 0.95 ) \beta=(0.9,0.95) , weight decay 0.05 0.05 ) at a peak learning rate of 3 × 10 − 4 3\times 10^{-4} , linearly warmed up over 500 500 steps and then cosine-annealed to zero, with gradients clipped to a global norm of 1.0 1.0 , in bf16, at a batch of eight windows ( 2,048 2{,}048 cells) per step and one accelerator per arm with arms run concurrently. The aggregator and the decoder share that learning rate; the only parameters on a separate schedule are the rotary and PoPE frequency grids, which carry a 0.1 × 0.1\times multiplier and so train at 3 × 10 − 5 3\times 10^{-5} , a choice we found necessary to prevent an early collapse of attention entropy. Rotary frequencies are initialised on a geometric grid spanning 10 ​ μ 10\,\mu m to 2 2\, mm with bearings uniform on [ 0 , π ) [0,\pi) . The main results use 50,000 50{,}000 steps; the positional-encoding comparison of § 4.2 and the six-seed replication use 18,000 18{,}000 steps on a narrower 948 948 -gene decoder vocabulary. The two budgets are identical in every optimisation setting above and differ only in the step count and hence in the cosine decay horizon, and their absolute values are not comparable, so no comparison in this paper crosses that boundary. Within each budget every arm is byte-identical in configuration and seed. Datasets and Evaluation details Training masks whole cells.

For a fraction ρ = 0.1 \rho=0.1 of each window we replace the cell token by a learned mask embedding while retaining the coordinate, so a masked cell’s output state 𝐳 i \mathbf{z}_{i} is a function of the cells around it, their positions and its own position, and of nothing else about it. A negative-binomial head decodes counts, with log ⁡ μ ^ i ​ g = [ MLP ⁡ ( 𝐳 i ) ] g + log ⁡ ς i \log\hat{\mu}_{ig}=[\mathrm{MLP}(\mathbf{z}_{i})]_{g}+\log\varsigma_{i} for library size ς i \varsigma_{i} , and the loss − ∑ i ∈ ℳ ∑ g log NB ( x i ​ g ∣ μ ^ i ​ g , ϕ g ) -\sum_{i\in\mathcal{M}}\sum_{g}\log\mathrm{NB}(x_{ig}\mid\hat{\mu}_{ig},\phi_{g}) is computed on masked cells only. Reconstructing a cell from its neighbourhood is an established objective family [ 8 , 32 , 34 ] . The task cannot be solved without geometry, since position is the only cell-specific information retained about a masked cell. Masking is applied after the frozen backbone and input projection: each masked cell’s projected embedding is replaced by a learned mask token before entering the spatial attention module, while its coordinates are retained (Fig. 1 ; Appendix D ). Thus, the masked cell’s own expression-derived embedding is not available to the spatial attention module. Measuring what a component buys usually means comparing a model against a re-implementation of a baseline, which mixes the mechanism under test with everything else two codebases differ in. We remove that confound structurally: the output projection of every inter-cell attention block is zero-initialised, so at step 0 0 the aggregator is the identity map and a model with a positional encoding emits outputs identical to one without. The observed deviation is exactly 0 0 on real checkpoints rather than merely within tolerance, and in the positional-encoding comparison of § 4.2 , all five configurations, including the geometry-free baseline, begin training at an identical loss to numerical precision.

Appendix I Benchmark protocol and full results The task list, the probe protocol, the validation gate and its threshold, the fit budget and the cell-intersection rule were all written before any baseline was staged. Two tasks were declared unevaluable in advance and are reported unevaluated rather than dropped. The cohort is 39 39 sections and 18,319,942 18{,}319{,}942 cells: 30 30 training sections on which probes are fitted, and nine held-out sections on which every number is scored. Cell ordering was verified against the cached representation on all 39 39 sections for every model. No model was scored until it passed a strict weight load with zero missing and zero unexpected tensors, an embedding rank equal to the model width, exact determinism on repeated embedding, and a gene-shuffle negative control; observed degradation fractions under the shuffle were 0.733 0.733 for Tessera , 0.818 0.818 for Nicheformer and 0.856 0.856 for scGPT-spatial, against a pre-registered bar of 0.50 0.50 . Every model is scored on the same 4,986,465 4{,}986{,}465 cells, an intersection over all models.

The 43,850 43{,}850 excluded cells are all ones scGPT-spatial cannot embed, because their counts over the matched panel are entirely zero and a frozen per-cell encoder that keeps only non-zero genes has nothing to tokenise. Such cells carry a missing row rather than a zero row, since a zero row is a fabricated embedding at the origin, and Tessera was denied those cells too. Niche composition and cell-type annotation require cell-type labels, which the nine held-out sections do not carry. Scoring them on the three labelled training sections was refused, since Tessera trained on those sections and the baselines did not. Neighbourhood density is the closest label-free substitute and is what we report. A third registered task, imputation through the shared linear probe, placed all three models below a constant predictor: one ridge cannot map a 512 512 -dimensional embedding onto a 1245 1245 -gene count vector, and it fails identically for all three, so we report a failed readout rather than a result and did not substitute a statistic that works better. Appendix K Limitations The backbone is frozen, so Tessera is an aggregator over a single-cell embedding rather than an end-to-end spatial foundation model, and its ceiling is that of the embedding it consumes. Unfreezing it did not change the result, but four factors change together between those two arms, so we register and report that comparison as descriptive rather than as an isolated measurement.
